about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

cotton.fundamental: Old-crop has bounced with Dec back to ~76 (+1.4%) and Mar near 80 despite a firm dollar, a technical recovery rather than new supply news. Dec deliveries and the high-grade share of certificated stock still cap the comfort for longs until Mar is the lead month.
events: Strong dollar weighed on cotton early (ADMIS)
Dec ~76.0, Mar ~79.8 by midday (ICE via TradingView)
Texas yield trimmed again in USDA's November report (RFD-TV)

sugar.fundamental: A sharp Brazil-led leg lower: the real slid another ~2% to ~5.90 per dollar and Mar raws dropped ~4.7% to ~17.2, a 7-week low, as a cheaper real favours Brazilian export pricing. India's early crush adds to the near-term supply feel; its fresh raw-sugar import tender is only a small offset.
events: Mar raws ~17.19 (-4.7%), below 17.92 and 17.23 supports (ICE via TradingView)
India invites fresh bids to import raw sugar (Reuters)

coffee.fundamental: Flat price is holding up (Dec ~280, Mar ~276) even with the real down ~2%, so producer selling is not overwhelming the market. Shrinking ICE certified arabica stocks keep Dec deliverability tight and remain the main support for the Dec/Mar spread.
events: Arabica near unchanged as the real weakens (ICE via TradingView)
Coffee and cocoa had slipped with sugar on Wednesday (Reuters)
ICE certified arabica stocks keep declining (ICE)

cocoa.fundamental: A strong rebound (Mar ~5,170, +3.4%) looks like short covering after the slide toward 4,980 support; the supply picture has not changed, with ICE stocks still climbing and West African prospects improved, so the bounce lacks fundamental backing.
events: Cocoa Mar up ~3.4% to ~5,173 (ICE via TradingView)
Soaring ICE inventories pressured prices on Wednesday (Barchart)
Ghana plans to phase out raw bean exports by 2030 (Reuters)
